To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) HIV infection accelerates the aging process, (2) HIV infection causes an accelerated aging process, and (3) the aging process accelerates the progression of HIV infection.
the HIV infection is a risk factor for frailty.
HIV infection and aging are both associated with a progressive loss of T cell function and that this loss is more rapid and pronounced in HIV-infected individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the immune response in HIV-infected patients and its relation to the aging process, with the aim of identifying new therapeutic strategies that could be useful in slowing down the progression of the disease.
the development of new drugs for the treatment of HIV infection and other viral infections.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the development of age-related diseases and the identification of novel therapeutic targets to improve the health and quality of life of the elderly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of geriatric HIV is still in its infancy.
HIV-infected elderly patients are a growing population experiencing an increased risk of age-related diseases.
HIV-infected elderly are not only a growing population experiencing an increasing risk for illnesses and geriatric syndres, but that HIV care and geriatric medicine will increasingly overlap.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system of HIV infected individuals is altered and this alteration can be accelerated by the infection.
the HIV infection is a complex and multi-factorial disease that affects the immune system, and this is the reason for its association with accelerated aging.
HIV infection accelerates the aging of the immune system, and the immune system in turn accelerates the process of aging in other systems of the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the era of ART, the HIV infection per se is not a risk factor for the development of frailty.
the immune system of the elderly HIV-infected patient is characterized by a high level of activation, which is associated with a high risk of developing non-AIDS events.
HIV infection is associated with an accelerated immune aging.
